=== page 3 ===
“Making speciality medicines accessible”, NATCO’s four-and-
a-half-decade journey has been driven by our commitment 
to expanding access to essential therapies. We continue to 
strengthen our global presence, led by our formulations export 
business and supported by a diversified portfolio. As part of our 
strategy to enter new markets and expand into newer therapies, 
we have entered the South African pharmaceutical market 
through the acquisition of 49%* stake in Adcock Ingram Holdings 
Proprietary Limited the second-largest (in terms of private market share) pharmaceutical company in South Africa.
As we venture into new frontiers, 
our commitment continues to shape our direction. Guided by operational excellence and an expanding global footprint, we are confident in our ability to create sustainable value. The pharmaceutical landscape is rapidly evolving, 
it is shaped by scientific breakthroughs, regulatory 
complexity, and driven by patient needs. The 
path to sustainable growth lies in exploring new 
horizons. Against this backdrop, we take this 
opportunity to reflect on our progress and our 
ambitions for the future, acknowledging the 
advances in the pharmaceutical industry globally 
and in India, while reaffirming our commitment to 
improving access to quality medicines. 
A significant step in this direction is the launch 
of generic Semaglutide injection in the form of 
vials making NATCO the first company to launch 
the most affordable GLP-1 in the market. By 
making advanced GLP-1 therapy more affordable, 
we are improving access and enabling better 
patient outcomes. We also launched Risdiplam 
injection (first generic) in India, which is used in 
the treatment for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) 
in paediatric and adult patients. By launching Risdiplam we have made the treatment more 
affordable and accessible for patients in India.
*On November 11, 2025, NATCO Pharma South Africa 
Proprietary Limited (“NPSA”) acquired 34.88% of Adcock 
Ingram Holdings Proprietary Limited (“Adcock Ingram”). 
Pursuant to this action, Adcock Ingram got delisted. Before 
delisting, NATCO Pharma Limited and NATCO Pharma 
(Canada) Inc. already held 0.12% and 0.75% of Adcock 
Ingram respectively. On a consolidated basis, NATCO 
ultimately owned 35.75% of Adcock Ingram. Later on in July 2026, NPSA acquired an additional shareholding of 
13.25% of Adcock Ingram resulting in ultimate ownership 
of shareholding of 49% by NATCO in Adcock Ingram on a 
consolidated basis.Behind every breakthrough is the collective strength of our 
scientific talent, strategic vision and manufacturing excellence, 
working together to make specialty medicines more accessible. 
Beyond our core business, we continue to create impact at the 
grassroots level through initiatives that empower communities 
and improve lives.
This journey 
is anchored in our belief that progress is driven by purpose.

notes thereto. The presented financial

the requirements of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (including the rules made 
thereunder), Indian Accounting 
Standards, the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations

About Us
Our operations are underpinned by 
best-in-class manufacturing and 
research facilities that meet evolving 
quality and compliance standards, 
enabling us to consistently address 
the expectations of our customers. 
Deep domain expertise, coupled with 
sustained investments in technology, 
has supported the steady expansion 
of our pharmaceutical business across 
global markets. Sustainability remains central to 
our approach to strategic markets, 
operational excellence, guiding the 
development of a more responsible and 
efficient manufacturing ecosystem. This 
commitment is reflected in our focus on 
resource conservation, environmental 
protection and social responsibility. Expanding Access to Niche 
and Complex Medicines
We are a research-focused pharmaceutical Company with an integrated business 
strategy spanning development, manufacturing and marketing of Finished Dosage 
Formulations (FDFs), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Agrochemicals. 
Backed by 4+ decades of industry experience, we have evolved into a global 
enterprise with presence in more than 50 countries through 13 subsidiaries, step-down 
subsidiaries and an Associate.
Mission and Purpose 
Making specialty medicines 
accessible to all

Strategic Investment in Adcock Ingram Holdings Proprietary Limited  
(earlier known as Adcock Ingram Holdings Limited)
Strengthening 
NATCO’s International 
Growth Platform
Acquired additional 
stake in Adcock 
Ingram Holdings in July 
2026, taking the total 
shareholding in Adcock 
to 49%. 
*includes existing investments
**in terms of private market shareHeadquartered in Johannesberg, South Africa, Adcock Ingram Holdings Proprietary 
Limited has a rich heritage dating back to 1890 with presence across the 
Prescription, Over-the-Counter (OTC), Hospital and Consumer Healthcare segments 
supported by a diversified portfolio of established brands and operates three 
manufacturing facilities in South Africa. Adcock Ingram also owns 49% of a joint 
venture in India with two manufacturing facilities located at Bangalore, India.In November 2025, NATCO Pharma South Africa Proprietary Limited (NPSA) completed the acquisition of a 34.88% stake in 
Adcock Ingram for a consideration of approximately ZAR 4.0 billion (about US$226 million). The transaction formed part of a 
scheme of arrangement through which Adcock Ingram was delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), transitioning 
the company into a privately held business with NATCO eventually holding 35.75% of Adcock Ingram on a consolidated basis. In 
July 2026, NPSA completed acquisition of an additional stake of 13.25% in Adcock Ingram for a consideration of ZAR 1.81 billion 
(about US$ 111 million). This resulted in NATCO ultimately holding 49% in Adcock Ingram on a consolidated basis. 
FY26 marked a significant strategic milestone for NATCO with the 
acquisition of a 35.75%* stake in Adcock Ingram, the second-largest 
pharmaceutical company in South Africa**. The investment established 
a strong strategic foothold in the African pharmaceutical market and 
strengthened NATCO’s international footprint. This strategic position 
was further deepened in the early part of FY27 with the acquisition 
of an additional 13.25% stake taking NATCO’s holding to 49% and 
reinforcing its long-term commitment to the African market.

Milestones 
Tracing the Arc of 
Our Evolution
Our journey reflects a sustained commitment to innovation, accessibility and responsibility, 
as we work towards building a healthier and more inclusive future. As we look ahead, we 
recognise the significant progress in healthcare globally and in India, while reaffirming our 
focus on improving access to quality medicine.
Since its incorporation in 1981, NATCO Pharma has evolved from a single-unit operation with a small team into a international 
pharmaceutical Company with a team of 5200+ globally. Today, with multiple manufacturing facilities, strong research capabilities 
and an expanding international presence, the organisation continues to progress with a clear and consistent purpose.

Chairman and CEO’s Message
Global Ambitions,  
Built on a Strong FoundationTo My fellow Shareholders,
NATCO was founded in 1981 with a 
simple but ambitious mission to provide 
and increase accessibility of specialty 
medicines in India. We pioneered 
a lot of first time generic medicine 
launches in India thereby improving 
accessibility and affordability to the 
therapy. While the world and industry 
have changed significantly since 
then, our core strategy has remained 
consistent over time where we continue 
to build a niche and complex pipeline 
of products. As a company, we have 
grown multi-fold over decades, from 
an INR 4,613 million total income in 
FY2010 to INR 43,759 million in FY26. 
Our Profit After Tax (After share of profit 
of Associate) in FY2010 was at INR 487 
million and in FY2026 it was INR 14,185 
million. Today we are a team of 5,200+ 
globally, working towards delivering 
measurable results, and adding value to 
the shareholders. 
Adcock Ingram Holdings Proprietary 
Limited, an Associate company of 
NATCO incorporated in South Africa 
reported US$ 592 million revenue with 
a PAT of US$ 57 million during financial 
year ending June 2026.
FY26 was a year that tested the 
resilience of the global pharmaceutical 
industry as much as it tested its 
ability to sustain growth. Geopolitical 
disruptions in the Middle East and 
tariff-related uncertainty in the U.S. 
added to the challenges. Overall, it was 
a challenging year of consolidation and 
reset for us, as we transitioned from a 
once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that had 
placed NATCO on a strong footing and 
further strengthened our balance sheet.
Navigating Cycles with Prudence
We closed the year with a healthy 
balance sheet, which gives us 
the flexibility to pursue growth. 
Formulation exports, our largest 
revenue contributor, will moderate 
in line with the Lenalidomide-led 
decline, while domestic formulations 
see a strong growth.
Building a More Diversified Growth 
Engine
Strategically, we are strengthening 
our base business to reduce our 
reliance on exclusivity-driven 
earnings. Two levers define this shift. 
First, geographic diversification: 
our earnings base today draws 
from five markets – India, the U.S., 
Brazil, Canada and, with this year’s 
acquisition, South Africa – compared 
to our earlier dependence on the U.S. 
alone. This year, we increased our 
holding in Indonesia, making it a wholly 
owned subsidiary. Second, portfolio 
diversification: our long-term ambition 
is for base-business revenue to 
contribute a larger share of profit, with 
first-to-file opportunities contributing to 
revenues rather than driving earnings. 
This year’s most significant step in 
this direction was the acquisition of a 
35.75% (including existing stake) stake 
in Adcock Ingram, the second largest 
pharmaceutical company in South 
Africa, that got subsequently increased 
to 49%. With this acquisition, the 
Group’s combined revenue crosses $1 
billion. It also gives us an established 
commercial platform in a market of 
scale, and we expect its contribution to build into steady, accretive earnings 
in the years to come.
Building Momentum 
The year saw several first-to-market 
and strategic milestones, like, the 
launch of generic Semaglutide multi-
dose vials in India at an affordable 
price point, positioning us as a first 
mover in this category, then the launch 
of Risdiplam for Spinal Muscular 
Atrophy, expanding access to a high-
cost rare-disease therapy, and in the 
U.S., the launch of Pomalidomide, 
Everolimus (1mg) and Bosentan. The 
launches in domestic business and 
expansion into new geographies will 
strengthen the base business. With an 
intent to sharpen strategic focus for 
the pharmaceutical business. With the 
focus on Agro chemical business it is 
expected to grow in revenues as well 
as profitability. We are demerging the 
crop health sciences business. The 
business thus will have an independent 
growth trajectory and will unlock value 
for the shareholders.
A Business Built on Balance and 
Strong Foundation
Export formulations remained 
our largest segment but saw the 
anticipated decline from the loss of 
Lenalidomide exclusivity. Domestic 
formulations grew steadily, led by 
oncology, cardiology, diabetology 
and our specialty divisions. Crop 
Health Sciences delivered growth, 
rising to INR 1,382 million in revenue 
from INR 606 million, aided by new 
product launches across categories A company’s true value can be 
measured by the lives it has 
touched. I am delighted by the 
efforts our team has put in over 
years. Giving back to community , 
NATCO Trust by its initiatives has 
over years worked on improving the 
early education, access to health 
and we remain committed in the 
inclusive development.V.C. Nannapaneni 
Chairman and Managing Director 
This phase is part of our long-
term strategy to build a diversified, 
globally distributed pharmaceutical 
company whose earnings are not 
dependent on any single product 
or market. We remain committed 
to disciplined capital allocation and 
continue to expand our platform, 
including through acquisitions that 
can strengthen our business in the 
years ahead.Rajeev Nannapaneni 
Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

surgeries in the year. The Road Ahead

years. We expect ‘double-digit earnings 
growth over the next two to three

of our international operations in Brazil, 
Canada, Emerging Markets including 
South Africa. ‘These businesses are 
adding to the strength of our platform

term strategy, focused on building 
a diversified, globally distributed 
pharmaceutical company whose 
earnings do not rest on any single 
event or market. We remain committed 
to disciplined capital allocation and 
continue to evaluate further acquisitions 
that can strengthen this platform in 
the years ahead.We thank our shareholders for their 
continued confidence, enduring trust 
and patience through a cyclical phase, 
our employees across geographies 
for their commitment and resilience, 
and our patients, doctors, partners 
regulators and financial institutions 
for the trust they continue to 
place in NATCO.

Balancing growth across base business 
by entering various markets across the

products requires a disciplined portfolio 
approach. The strategy is to expand 
core revenue streams while investing 
in high value niche opportunities and 
leveraging commodities for volume, 
market presence.
Drive sustainable revenue and 
profitability growth by strengthening the 
base business, entering new markets, 
accelerating expansion in high-value 
niche products, and maximizing 
opportunities across segments. Our 
focus will be on increasing market 
share, and enhancing operational 
efficiency. Niche products offer 
differentiation, higher margins, and 
reduced competitive pressure. These 
products will be positioned as strategic 
growth drivers. Commodity products

strategy is to compete efficiently while 
protecting margins.

Overview of the entity’s material responsible business conduct issues
Material responsible business conduct and sustainability issues pertaining to environmental and social matters that present a 
risk or an opportunity to your business, rationale for identifying the same, approach to adapt or mitigate the risk along-with its 
financial implications.
1Energy and 
emissionsOpportunity We have established targets to reduce GHG emissions across our operations, 
supported by key initiatives such as procurement of renewable electricity, 
deployment of captive solar energy systems and the utilization of briquette-fired 
boilers to achieve these reductions.We aim to increase our percentage of renewable 
energy share to 35% by the end of 2035. Along 
with that, our goal is to become carbon neutral 
by 2050.Positive:  Key inherent benefits include 
optimization of overall energy costs and a 
reduction in emissions.Natural 
Capital
2Water  
managementRisk and 
OpportunityRisk:  Water is essential for pharmaceutical manufacturing and is a main input in 
the production, formulation and processing of APIs, intermediates and finished 
products. It is also extensively utilized in manufacturing and cleaning operations. 
Accordingly, effective water management is essential to our operational efficiency 
and sustainability.
Opportunity: We are committed to responsible water stewardship across all our 
facilities. We are addressing the risks associated with water scarcity, pollution and 
regulatory compliance while contributing to long term sustainability of its operations 
and communities we serve through continuous monitoring and optimization of water 
consumption, wastewater treatment and recycling, rooftop rainwater collection and 
reuse, rainwater harvesting, reuse and recharge systems at our facilities.We have recycled 47.10% of water in FY 
2025-26 at our facilities. Our key initiatives in 
water stewardship include adoption of water 
saving technologies, ensuring compliance with 
regulations. Monitoring water consumption, 
treatment and recycling of wastewater as well 
as rainwater harvesting.Negative:  Costs associated with water 
scarcity, pollution, and regulatory non-
compliance, including potential fines and 
penalties.
Positive:  It reflects a strong financial 
outlook, supported by our efforts to reduce 
costs and optimize water usage.Natural 
Capital
3Climate change Risk and 
OpportunityRisk:  Extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and regulatory changes 
associated with climate change pose risks to operations, supply chains, and 
infrastructure.
Opportunity:  It further enables opportunities in product innovation, energy 
efficiency improvements, and wider adoption of renewable energy.Our goal is to reach 35% renewable energy in 
our energy mix by 2035 and carbon neutrality 
by 2050. 
In FY 2025-26, we achieved 26.31% of RE in 
our energy mix.Negative:  Financial impacts of climate-
related damages and regulatory compliance 
obligations.
Positive:  Managing climate-related risks to 
minimize associated financial losses.Natural 
Capital
4Waste management Risk Non-compliance in waste management and environmental standards can lead to 
environmental harm, legal liabilities, financial penalties, and reputational damage.
We are committed to responsible waste management practices through waste 
minimization, segregation, reuse, recycle wherever practicable and disposing the 
wastes to the authorized recyclers/re-processorsWe ensure our production facilities operate in 
line with established standards by adhering to 
best practices. We are committed to minimizing 
waste generation, across operations, while 
promoting recycling and reuse and reducing 
landfill dependency.Negative:  Costs incurred from waste 
disposal, regulatory penalties, and 
environmental remediation activities.Natural 
Capital

OpportunityRisk:  Health and safety incidents may lead to production disruptions and

Opportunity:  Enhancing Competitive Advantage through a “Culture of Care.” 
By pivoting from regulatory compliance to a holistic wellbeing strategy—
encompassing both physical and mental health. Proactive investments in health 
and safety directly reduce employee turnover, lower recruitment costs, and boost 
overall workforce engagement and productivity.We have implemented a robust EHS policy

45001:2018 OHS management systems.Negative:  Costs arising from workplace 
incidents, such as medical expenses, legal

resulting in loss of productivity. 
Positive:  Reduced downtime through 
efficient systems and processes in place. Human

Risk Management 
The Discipline of 
Preparedness
The risks inherent in the pharmaceutical industry carry significant consequences, 
making effective risk management essential to ensuring patient safety, meeting stringent 
regulatory standards and safeguarding brand reputation. Failure to manage these risks 
can result in patient harm, legal liabilities and regulatory sanctions. 
We regard strategic risk management as fundamental to building long-term resilience, strengthening stakeholder trust and 
enabling sustainable growth. Through a robust, multi-layered framework, we anticipate challenges, safeguard opportunities 
and consistently uphold our commitments to patients, investors and society at large. Risk Management Process
Risk Identification 
We recognise and list 
potential internal and 
external risks that may 
impact our operationsRisk Assessment 
We evaluate the 
likelihood and impact 
of identified risks to 
prioritise them effectivelyRegulatory Alignment

comply with applicable 
legal and industry 
regulations

We determine the extent 
of risk we are prepared 
to accept while pursuing 
our objectivesProactive Mitigation
We implement strategies 
and actions to reduce or 
eliminate the impact of 
key risksOngoing Monitoring
We use structured 
frameworks to review, 
monitor and refine our risk 
responses continuously01 02 03 04 05 06

Governance 
Where Deep Insight 
Meets ForesightOur Committees
Board Composition and Expertise 
Composition Areas of Expertise In a rapidly evolving and highly competitive business environment, strong governance 
serves as a critical differentiator. At the core of our organisation is an experienced 
Board of Directors, providing strategic direction, navigating challenges and fostering 
a culture of innovation and continuous improvement. Integrity remains central to 
everything we do, guiding our commitment to consistent and sustainable progress. 
This is reinforced by a robust governance framework, supported by well-defined

4,086 10.5Our NCE and Cell and Gene Therapy Investments
Innovation and research form a critical pillar of our long-term growth 
strategy as we expand our presence across New Chemical Entities 
(NCEs), cell and gene therapy platforms, regenerative medicine 
and advanced biologics. Through strategic investments, targeted 
collaborations and focused R&D initiatives, we are building a diversified 
innovation ecosystem that enables us to meet global healthcare needs.
eGenesis
We invested US$ 8 million in eGenesis, a biotechnology company 
focused on xenotransplantation through the development of safe 
and effective human-compatible organs for transplant. The company 
achieved a significant milestone with the first human transplant of a 
genetically engineered pig kidney in March 2024 and is advancing 
programmes across kidney, liver and heart transplantation to address 
global organ shortage challenges.
NRC – 2694
NRC-2694-A is an orally administered small-molecule tyrosine kinase 
inhibitor discovered and developed by NATCO Pharma Limited. The 
molecule is being evaluated for recurrent or metastatic head and 
neck cancer in patients progressing on pembrolizumab therapy; 
Applied for permissions to start phase II clinical trials in the US.
Cellogen Therapeutics
We invested US$ 2 million in Cellogen Therapeutics, which focuses 
on advanced cellular engineering methods and gene-therapy-based 
approaches. The company is developing innovative third and fourth 
generation CAR-T cell therapies for leukemia and lymphoma, along with 
genetic therapies for beta-thalassemia and sickle cell disease. Cellogen 
Therapeutics has also received GMP manufacturing approvals in India.
Stero Therapeutics
We invested US$ 1 million in Stero Therapeutics, which is developing 
novel therapies for metabolic diseases. The company is currently 
focused on therapies for Cushing’s syndrome and expanding into NASH-
related treatments, supported by ongoing pre-clinical animal studies.

Economic Overview
Global Economy1
The global economy remained stable in CY2025, growing by 3.3%, supported by sustained private investment and easing inflation. 
Growth divergence persisted, with emerging markets and developing economies expanding by 4.4%, compared to 1.7% in 
advanced economies. A relatively weaker US dollar and coordinated monetary conditions supported capital flows and demand in 
developing markets.

Global Economic Outlook
Global trade expansion is expected to moderate as the benefits 
of supply chain reconfiguration stabilise and the impact of 
tariffs gradually feed into end-market pricing. China‘s efforts 
to address excess capacity are likely to increase its focus on 
domestic demand while maintaining strong trade linkages 
across Asian supply chains. 
Geopolitical uncertainty remains a key risk, requiring 
companies to maintain flexibility through diversified sourcing 
and regionalised supply chains.
Investment in artificial intelligence is expected to remain 
strong, supported by its demonstrated impact on productivity 
and operational efficiency. Its growing application in demand 
forecasting, inventory optimisation and process automation is 
improving cost control across industries.

Source –  IMF WEO April 2026Indian Economy2
India’s economy remained resilient in FY 2025-26, recording 
GDP growth of 7.7% despite external uncertainties3. Inflation 
moderated, supported primarily by stable food prices and 
improved supply conditions. This created room for the Reserve 
Bank of India to ease monetary policy, with a cumulative rate 
cut of 100 basis points to 5.25%, improving overall liquidity and 
credit conditions.
Manufacturing activity remained strong, with the Purchasing 
Manager’s Index (PMI) indicating sustained expansion, 
driven by healthy order flows and productivity improvements. 
Industrial production recovered during the year, supported by 
improved output in automobiles, basic metals and mining. 
Consumption trends strengthened, with private final 
consumption expenditure increasing by over 7%. This was 
supported by a resurgence in rural demand and declining 
inflation. Policy measures, including GST rationalisation, also 
contributed to improved consumption patterns, particularly 
in urban markets.
Structural efforts to strengthen India’s innovation ecosystem 
continued. The government’s Research Development and 
Innovation (RDI) scheme, with an outlay of H 1 lakh Crore, is 
aimed at increasing private sector participation in advanced 
manufacturing and technology development.4
Indian Economic Outlook
India's growth momentum is expected to remain stable. A 
gradual rebound in the manufacturing activity, along with 
ongoing structural reforms, is expected to help navigate 
external uncertainties. 
Infrastructure investment remains a key driver. The Union 
Budget for FY 2026-27 provides for an 11.5% increase in 
capital expenditure to H12.22 lakh Crore, reinforcing the focus 
on long-term capacity creation and economic expansion. 
Recent and proposed free trade agreements, including those 
with the European Union and New Zealand, are expected to 
improve market access for Indian exporters. These agreements 
are likely to support export growth and attract foreign 
investment, particularly in sectors such as pharmaceuticals.

7Global obesity medicine spending increased sharply between 2023 
and 2024, driven by the adoption of innovative therapies. Obesity-

incremental market opportunity of approximately $50.7 billion. The 
base-case outlook estimates the global obesity medicines market 
at approximately $77 billion by 2029, while broader adoption and 
reimbursement expansion could support a higher market scenario 
of up to $118 billion. Growing awareness of metabolic health and 
increasing treatment penetration are expected to support sustained 
long-term demand for obesity therapies.
Regional Analysis
LATAM and Asia-Pacific
Growth across Latin America is expected to remain strong through 
2029, supported by improving healthcare access, rising chronic 
disease prevalence and sustained pharmaceutical demand 
across key markets such as Brazil and Mexico. Alongside Asia-
Pacific markets, the region is projected to record faster growth in 
medicine usage and spending compared to several developed 
economies. Over the past five years, global patient usage of 
medicines increased by 14%, driven in part by expanding 
healthcare access across China, Asia-Pacific and Latin America. 
CAR-T Cell Therapies (CAR-Ts)
Representing the leading edge of personalised oncology, 
CAR-T therapies involve extracting a patient’s own T cells, 
genetically modifying them and re-infusing them to target 
and destroy malignant cells with exceptional precision.
In CY 2025, this modality generated $5.8 billion  in sales, 
with projections reaching $8 billion  by CY 2030.

=== page 56 ===
In Brazil, continued growth is supported by rising healthcare 
expenditure, expanding treatment access and increasing 
demand for chronic disease therapies. Meanwhile, Canada’s 
pharmaceutical market continues to evolve through pricing 
reforms, broader biosimilar adoption and changing healthcare 
delivery models aimed at improving system efficiency and 
managing public healthcare costs.
Southeast Asia
Across Southeast Asia, rising incomes and an expanding 
middle class are shifting consumer preferences towards more 
convenient, high-quality and personalised healthcare services. 
To meet this evolving demand, the Association of Southeast 
Asian Nations (ASEAN) is advancing its Pharmaceutical 
Regulatory Policy to harmonise regional standards, promote 
intra-bloc trade and reduce import reliance. 
Within the region, specific markets are scaling rapidly. 
Indonesia's pharmaceutical sector is expanding, supported 
by the world’s largest single-payer national health insurance 
system, while Vietnam and Thailand are leveraging robust 
research hospital networks to become premier clinical trial 
destinations. Concurrently, the Philippines has emerged as a 
leading market for international pharmaceutical firms seeking 
to establish regional presence.
United States
The U.S. pharmaceutical market is projected to grow at a CAGR 
of 3–6% on a net price basis through 2029, reflecting moderation 
compared to the stronger growth recorded over the previous 
five-year period. Despite the normalization in percentage growth, 
net medicine spending is still expected to increase substantially, 
rising from approximately $487 billion in 2024 to nearly $800 
billion by 2029. Growth is expected to be driven by continued 
adoption of innovative therapies across oncology, immunology, 
neurology, obesity and diabetes treatment segments. At the same 
time, the industry is expected to witness increasing pressure 
from patent expiries and biosimilar competition, which are likely 
to intensify pricing pressures while creating opportunities for 
generic and lower-cost therapeutic alternatives.
Europe
Pharmaceutical spending across Europe is projected to 
increase by approximately $85 billion through 2029, supported 
by continued demand for innovative therapies as well as

established branded treatments. Growth within the region is 
expected to be driven primarily by the EU4 markets and the 
UK, with increasing adoption of specialty medicines across 
oncology, immunology and rare disease therapies. In addition, 
Germany continues to demonstrate one of the fastest uptake 
rates for innovative pharmaceutical launches among major 
global markets, reflecting strong access to new therapies and 
a supportive commercial environment.
At the same time, the European pharmaceutical market 
continues to operate within a highly regulated pricing and 
reimbursement framework. Ongoing healthcare policy 
initiatives aimed at strengthening healthcare preparedness, 
accelerating clinical development and improving access to 
innovative medicines are expected to support long-term market 
expansion. However, continued pricing pressure from patent 
expiries, biosimilar competition and broader healthcare cost-
containment measures across public healthcare systems may 
moderate overall market value growth over the forecast period.
South Africa*
South Africa’s pharmaceutical market is the largest and most 
mature in sub-Saharan Africa, valued at approximately USD 8.3 
billion and projected to reach up to USD 12.4 billion by 2033. 
The market is expected to grow at a Compound Annual Growth 
Rate (CAGR) of 5.2% to 5.5%. Driven by cost containment and 
government mandates, it features a strong demand for generic 
drugs and a rapidly growing biologics sector. Conventional 
small-molecule drugs dominate, but biologics and biosimilars 
represent the fastest-growing segment. The high cost of 
patented drugs and single-exit pricing policies push strong 
utilization of generic medicines. High demand for treatments 
targeting HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis (TB), cancer, and lifestyle-
related chronic diseases.
Outlook
Global medicine spending is projected to exceed $2.6 trillion 
over the next five years, growing at a CAGR of 5-8%. The 
US is expected to remain the largest contributor to global 
pharmaceutical expenditure.

Indian Pharmaceutical Industry
India has established itself as the ‘pharmacy of the world’ 
by supplying affordable, -quality generics and vaccines to 
developing and regulated markets. It ranks 3rd globally by 
volume and 11th by value, with the market valued at $ 60 
billion in 2025. India has the world's highest number of US-
FDA-compliant pharmaceutical manufacturing plants outside 
of the United States. Its API sector ranks as the third largest 
globally, supplying 57% of the API listed on the WHO Model 
List of Essential Medicines.10
The domestic industry is experiencing a structural transition 
toward a value-driven paradigm, expanding its footprint into 
complex generics, specialty medicines, biosimilars, and 
high-tech medical devices. Total pharmaceutical exports 
neared the $30.5 billion threshold, with approximately 50% of 
shipments directed to highly regulated markets like the United 
States and Europe.11
To reduce import dependence on critical bulk drugs and 
intermediates, the production capacity for 26 key APIs has 
been expanded under the central Production Linked Incentive 
(PLI) framework, attracting substantial domestic capital and 
generating extensive employment. Along with APIs, the H 15,000 
crore outlay programme incentivises the commercialisation of specialized therapeutic formulations, including advanced 
anti-cancer, anti-diabetic and cardiovascular drugs, moving 
Indian players up the global value chain.This manufacturing 
resilience is further augmented by a significant allocation in 
the Union Budget for the Department of Pharmaceuticals, 
which includes strategic fiscal outlays to promote centralized 
bulk drug and medical device parks across multiple states, 
positioning the country to capture higher-value segments in 
global healthcare commerce.
India is the largest supplier of generic medicines globally, 
accounting for-
of global generics supply of the global API industry20% 8%
Government Initiatives
Production Linked Incentive Scheme
The PLI schemes by the Department of Pharmaceuticals are 
critical to boosting domestic manufacturing and reducing 
import dependence. They have already helped eliminate 
imports worth H 3,591 Crore across APIs, KSMs and DIs.
PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals
Focused on high-value biopharmaceuticals, complex generics 
and autoimmune medicines, the scheme has driven growth 
in sales, exports and employment. As of September 2025, 
investments stood at H 40,890 crore, leading to employment 
generation of around 97,000 jobs.
Research and Innovation
The Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma MedTech 
(PRIP) scheme aims to transition India from a generics-led to an 
innovation-driven economy. Seven Centres of Excellence have 
been established within the National Institutes of Pharmaceutical 
Education and Research (NIPER) with an expenditure of  
H 700 crores. The PRIP scheme provides financial support to 
MSMEs, startups and other industries working towards critical 
pharmaceutical and medtech research.
Biopharma Strategy for Healthcare Advancement through 
Knowledge, Technology and Innovation (SHAKTI)
Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, this scheme has 
an outlay of H 10,000 crores over the next five years. It aims 
to position India as a global biologics manufacturing hub, 
accelerating innovation and advanced biopharma capabilities.

Outlook
As the industry evolves, the focus is shifting from cost-driven manufacturing to innovation and R&D-driven growth. Strengthening 
intellectual property protection and regulatory transparency will be critical to attracting early-stage research and fostering innovation. 
India’s policy framework continues to support domestic manufacturing of key starting materials (KSMs), drug intermediates 
and APIs, encouraging greater self-reliance and strengthening the pharmaceutical supply chain. Going forward, the industry is 
expected to maintain a steady growth trajectory, supported by favourable policies, rising healthcare demand and expanding 
manufacturing capabilities.
Crop Protection
The Indian crop protection chemicals market is projected to increase from $2.59 billion in 2025 to $2.71 billion in 2026, supported 
by a gradual shift towards organised players. Growth is driven by precision agriculture adoption, supportive government policies 
and an increasing focus on sustainable practices. 
Primary growth drivers of the industry 
include Precision and sustainable 
agriculture:  Expanding adoption of 
precision spraying technologies and a 
strategic transition toward Integrated 
Pest Management (IPM) protocols.Risk mitigation:  A heightened focus on 
managing agro-climatic risks, alongside 
regulatory tailwinds that favour the 
adoption of safer, modern chemistries.Growth Headroom:  Relatively low 
baseline per-hectare consumption 
signals significant potential for targeted 
volume and value expansion.
Global Supply Chain Realignment: 
India’s emergence as a preferred 
international sourcing hub, 
supported by expanding technical 
capacities and global businesses 
diversifying their supply chains.Structural Labour Dynamics: 
Acute rural labour shortages are 
accelerating the transition towards 
chemical crop protection delivery as 
a more cost-effective and efficient 
alternative to manual application.
Production in FY 2025-26 reached 2,61,099 MT (up to February 
2026), significantly exceeding the estimated demand of 74,266 
MT, of which 42,000 MT is expected to be consumed during 
the Kharif 2026 season.
Government initiatives such as the $338 million Digital 
Agriculture Mission are accelerating demand for technologies 
compatible with drones and soil mapping. At the same time, 
structural challenges persist, including molecule bans across states, spurious chemicals and stringent residue regulations. 
Enforcement against counterfeit and substandard pesticides 
is strengthening, with closer coordination between central and 
state authorities. 
Farmers are gradually shifting from conventional spraying to 
precision application techniques, improving input efficiency 
and aligning with environmental standards.

Company Overview
NATCO Pharma Ltd is an integrated, research-driven 
pharmaceutical company with over four decades of experience, 
focused on developing niche and complex molecules. Over 
the decades it has evolved to become one of the globally 
diversified pharmaceutical companies. The Company has also 
diversified into crop health sciences, offering agrochemical 
solutions in the Indian market. Its operations span Finished 
Dosage Formulations (FDF), Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients 
(API) and agrochemicals (technical and formulations). It is 
highly regarded as one of the pioneers in the Indian oncology 
therapeutic segment, where the company has launched 
many first-time generic cancer products.  The API business 
specialises in multi-stage synthesis, high-potency APIs and 
peptides, largely for captive consumption.
The Company operates nine cutting-edge manufacturing 
facilities in India—seven for pharmaceuticals and two 
for agrochemicals, all compliant with various regulatory 
standards including USFDA, ANVISA, Health Canada and 
WHO. Formulation plants are situated in Dehradun (Himachal 
Pradesh), Kothur (Telangana), Nagarjuna Sagar (Telangana), 
Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Guwahati (Assam); API 
units are established in Mekaguda (Telangana) and Manali 
(Tamil Nadu) while the agrochemical production facilities are in 
Attivaram (Andhra Pradesh). It has a wide range of formulations 
portfolio includes capsules, injections, tablets and other dosage 
forms addressing various therapeutic areas such as Oncology, 
Neurology, Gastroenterology, Cardiology, Diabetes and others.
NATCO has a presence in over 50 countries, with major 
markets including the US, India, Canada and Brazil, supported 
by 13 subsidiaries/step-down subsidiaries and an Associate 
and strategic alliances across regions such as Southeast Asia, 
LATAM and the Middle East. 
A major growth pillar is its R&D, with annual investments of H 
4,086 million (FY 2025-26) and a planned allocation of 6-8% 
of revenues toward future innovation. The Company focuses 
on low-competition, high-complexity molecules, leveraging 
organic expansion strategies. 
The formulation business, especially exports, accounts for 
the majority of revenues, while the APIs segment provides 
backward integration through cutting-edge manufacturing 
capabilities. In agrochemicals, the Crop Health Sciences 
division has established a strong position with CTPR & its 
combination products in India, well supported by the herbicides 
and growth promoter products in the portfolio. 
NATCO is committed to maintain cGMP standards across 
its facilities and endeavours to keep with the evolving 
regulatory landscape.  
On November 11, 2025, NATCO Pharma South Africa Proprietary 
Limited ("NPSA") acquired 34.88% of Adcock Ingram Holdings 
Proprietary Limited ("Adcock Ingram"). Pursuant to this action, 
Adcock Ingram got delisted. Before delisting, NATCO Pharma 
Limited and NATCO Pharma (Canada) Inc. already held 0.12% 
and 0.75% of Adcock Ingram respectively. On a consolidated 
basis, NATCO ultimately owned 35.75% of Adcock Ingram. 
Later on in July 2026, NPSA acquired an additional shareholding 
of 13.25% of Adcock Ingram resulting in ultimate ownership 
of shareholding of 49% by NATCO in Adcock Ingram on a 
consolidated basis.

Segment-wise Performance
The Company operates through two primary segments— 
Pharmaceuticals and Agrochemicals. The pharmaceutical 
business serves as the main revenue driver, led by export 
formulations, followed by domestic formulations, Active 
Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Agrochemicals.
The Company has established a notable global footprint, 
shipping formulation products to over fifty countries. The 
United States is the largest revenue contributor, followed by 
India, Canada and Brazil.
The API division is strategic in nature in order to cater to captive 
consumption and to ensure uninterrupted supply of products. 
It also sells to global pharmaceutical companies in USA, Brazil, 
Europe and India. 
Leveraging proficiency in organic chemistry and the ability to 
target niche molecules, the company diversified into the Crop 
protection  business. The product portfolio includes a range 
of quality pesticides, insecticides, bio-stimulants, and growth 
promoters designed for the safe and efficient management of 
pests, insects, diseases and weeds across various crops. The 
Company remains focused on providing greener and cleaner 
solutions to farmers to enhance crop outputs.
Pharmaceutical Segment
The domestic pharmaceutical business is organised into 
four specialised Divisions: 
Oncology Pharma Specialty, Cardiology, Diabetology. These 
divisions are designed to address critical therapeutic areas 
through innovation, affordability, and quality, thereby improving 
patient benefits with advanced treatments.
Oncology
As a pioneer in oncology targeted therapy. The portfolio includes 
treatments for solid tumours and hemato-oncology. The current 
pipeline features molecules for various malignancies, including 
liver, lung and breast cancers.
The Company’s oncology products are manufactured in state-
of-the-art facilities certified by major international regulatory 
authorities. This commitment to quality and reliability has 
earned the trust of oncologists, leading medical centres and 
the broader healthcare community.
Pharma Specialty
Under pharma specialty two divisions have been created. 
Dynami and Hygeia.Dynami 
Dynami business unit focuses on the anti-infectives segment, 
covering a comprehensive portfolio of Antibacterials, 
Antifungals, Antivirals.
The division engages with key specialists, including Infectious 
Disease experts, Intensivists, Pulmonologists, and Bone 
Marrow Transplant (BMT) physicians.
Natco is actively investing in building a future-ready portfolio 
to address emerging challenges in infectious diseases and 
antimicrobial resistance.
Hygeia
The division also caters to multiple specialties, including 
Gastroenterology, Hepatology, Rheumatology, Orthopaedics, 
Paediatric Neurology and critical care.
Key milestones in FY 25-26 include launch of Risdiplam 
for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA), significantly improving 
medicine access in India. 
The orthopaedics portfolio includes leading oral and injectable 
bisphosphonate therapies, which were first-to-market in their 
categories. In gastro-hepatology, NATCO is a dominant player 
in Hepatitis-B and Hepatitis-C treatments in India, with the 
Velpanat brand (Sofosbuvir and combination) being a high-
performing product.
Cardiology
Established in 2017, the Cardiology division focuses on 
making specialty cardiovascular therapies widely accessible 
and affordable. The portfolio includes Antihypertensives, 
Antiplatelets, Novel Oral Anticoagulants
NATCO has achieved first-to-market status for key molecules 
such as Apixaban, Dabigatran. The division continues to 
expand its offerings with a focus on innovative and cost-
effective treatment options for cardiovascular diseases.
Diabetology
NATCO's Diabetology segment offers a comprehensive range 
of therapies for diabetes management, including DPP-4 
inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors. The Company is the first Indian 
generic manufacturer to launch Semaglutide injection for Type 
2 Diabetes Mellitus, available in both injection and pen delivery 
formats. Natco remains committed to strengthening this 
segment through development of next-generation therapies, 
with a focus on patient-centric innovation
NATCO Pharma’s India business is anchored in Therapeutic 
leadership across specialty segments, First-to-market 
innovations, High-quality manufacturing standards, Improved 
accessibility and affordability of treatment, these strategic 
initiatives reinforce Natco’s commitment to advancing healthcare 
outcomes and addressing critical patient needs across India.

COMPANY OVERVIEW
NATCO has two business segments, Pharmaceuticals and 
Agrochemicals. Pharmaceuticals constitute a major portion 
of the revenue, where export formulations contribute a major 
portion of the pharmaceutical’s revenue followed by API. 
Export formulations business focuses on high entry barrier 
and complex products and comprises of customers in US, 
Canada, Brazil, Asia-Pacific and other countries. API business 
is backward integrated making the business strategic in nature by serving its captive requirements. Capabilities in APIs 
include complex multi-step synthesis & scale-up, advanced 
synthetic/ separation technologies, containment facility for 
handling high potency APIs, synthesis of peptide (solid phase 
pharmaceuticals, oligo nucleotide pharmaceuticals etc., and 
a well-established process safety engineering lab. Our R&D 
capabilities are demonstrated by complex and niche product 
filings in formulations and API segments. Agrochemicals 
business segment is carried under Crop Health Sciences 
division of the Company. It has successfully launched broad-
spectrum insecticide Chlorantraniliprole (CTPR) and its 
combination products in India across key agrarian states. It 
is focused on establishing a product portfolio through crop 
phenology analysis and also explore export opportunities.

DEMERGER
The Company is inter alia engaged in two business verticals, 
namely: the Pharmaceutical Undertaking and the Agrochemicals 
Undertaking. The Company believe that the risk and reward 
associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are 
different. In order to segregate the Agrochemicals Undertaking 
with that of Pharmaceutical Undertaking, it is intended to 
demerge the Agrochemicals Undertaking on a going concern 
basis into the Wholly owned Subsidiary of the Company i.e., 
Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited (NCHSL).  The Company 
intends to retain the current shareholding in NCHSL in order 
to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business 
which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring 
the progress and providing strategic support.
The demerger, transfer and vesting of the Agrochemicals 
Undertaking on a going concern basis to NCHSL would result 
in better and efficient control by the management for the 
segregated businesses and promote their growth. Further, it 
would also result in the following benefits:	 The demerger would facilitate focused growth, operational 
efficiencies, business synergies and increased operational 
and customer focus in relation to the Agrochemicals 
Undertaking in the Resulting Company (i.e.. NCHSL) 
and the Pharmaceutical Undertaking in the Demerged 
Company. The demerger would thus provide a platform 
for having a concentrated approach towards development 
of the respective business verticals.
	 Focused business approach for the maximization of 
benefits to all the shareholders and opportunities for growth.
	 Operational rationalization, organization efficiency and 
optimum utilization of various resources
	 Ability to leverage financial and operational resources 
of each business.
	 Each business would be able to address independent 
business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation 
and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, 
lenders and other stakeholders.
	 The proposed demerger will enhance value for 
shareholders and allow a focused strategy in operation 
of the respective business verticals which would be in the 
best interest of the Demerged Company and the Resulting 
Company, shareholders, creditors and all persons 
connected therewith.
	 The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of 
the business verticals of the Demerged Company.
Upon the Scheme becoming effective and in consideration of 
the transfer and vesting of the Demerged Undertaking from 
the Demerged Company to the Resulting Company in terms 
of the Scheme, the Resulting Company shall, issue and allot 
equity shares, to all the members of the Demerged Company, 
holding fully paid-up equity shares on the Record Date in the 
following manner:
“1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of INR 2/- (Rupee Two only) 
each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted for 
every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of INR 2/- (Rupee Two 
only) each held in NATCO Pharma Limited”.

MATERIAL SUBSIDIARIES
As per Regulation 16(c) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing 
Regulations”), a “material subsidiary” to mean a subsidiary, 
whose turnover or net worth exceeds ten percent of the 
consolidated turnover or net worth respectively, of the listed 
entity and its subsidiaries in the immediately preceding 
accounting year. None of the Subsidiary Companies are 
material subsidiary to the Company based on the turnover or 
net worth as on 31st March, 2026.
In addition to the above, Regulation 24 of the Listing Regulations 
requires that at least one Independent Director on the Board 
of Directors of the listed entity shall be a Director on the 
Board of Directors of an unlisted material subsidiary, whether 
incorporated in India or not. For the purpose of this Regulation, 
material subsidiary means a subsidiary, whose turnover or net 
worth exceeds twenty percent of the consolidated turnover or 
net worth respectively, of the listed entity and its subsidiaries 
in the immediately preceding accounting year. Accordingly, the 
said provision of the appointment of an Independent Director of 
the Company in the Board of the material subsidiary Company 
is not applicable, since, the prescribed limits are not exceeded 
by the Company. 
The other requirements of Regulation 24 of the Listing 
Regulations with regard to Corporate Governance requirements 
for Subsidiary Companies have been complied with.

Conservation of Energy, Research and Development, Technology Absorption, Foreign Exchange 
Earnings and Outgo
A) CONSERVATION OF ENERGY:
(a) During the year, the Company has implemented energy conservation projects across its various business units. A few of the 
key initiatives include:
 1. Installation of Energy efficient equipment & optimization of processes consuming energy:
  Installed new high efficiency Utility equipment & improvise the operation of    existing utility system during the last fiscal 
and achieved significant saving in various utility areas resulted in reduction of 5498 Ton of CO2 emissions
 2. Identifying cheaper power sources both in-house and external and Utilizing the alternate sources of energy:
  (a) Increased utilization of alternate renewable   sources of energy by 8% using Dry oil Cake instead of Coal resulting 
in reduction of 2281 Ton of Co2 emission & Installed Solar Plant (565KW) to reduce Co2 emission by 905 Ton /Year
  (b) Installed high efficiency solar panel to achieve the saving of INR 9 Million/ annum.
 3. Steps in progress for increasing the utilization of alternate renewable sources of energy: 
  a) Propose to install 1.5 Mw Solar plant with Electrical Boiler / Battery Storage at Mekaguda.
   Expected saving per annum is approximately INR 22.8 Million.
B) TECHNOLOGY ABSORPTION
 Our R&D team has successfully developed an alternative synthetic route for key intermediate stages of the Apixaban production 
process. A comprehensive Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was conducted on the revised process, which demonstrated a 
potential reduction in overall environmental attributes by approximately 50% compared to the existing route.

Corporate Governance Report
Philosophy on Corporate Governance
NATCO Pharma Limited (NATCO) believes that good and 
responsible corporate governance is the backbone for 
sustainable performance, achieving long-term sustainable 
growth and enhancing stakeholder value. At NATCO, we believe 
that transparency in the form of disclosures, presence of strong 
Board with adequate composition of Independent Directors, 
compliance of law in letter and spirit, responsible corporate 
conduct and being accountable ensures good Corporate 
Governance and enhances the reputation of the Company 
globally without hindering with the shareholder’s faith in the 
Company. We being a global pharmaceutical company, driven 
by our mission “Making specialty medicines accessible” we 
strive to provide quality and affordable healthcare to patients 
globally. This purpose guides our organizational decisions and 
anchors our every action. This is our road path to consistent, 
competitive, profitable and responsible growth which creates a 
long-term value to our shareholders/ stakeholders.
Compliance Report on Corporate Governance
Your Company submits compliance report on Corporate 
Governance to the Stock Exchanges on quarterly, half-yearly 
and annual basis within the statutory time limits.

the Company in arriving at judicious decisions by exercising

The Company is in strict compliance of the Listing Regulations pertaining to disclosure of Audited/ Unaudited quarterly, half-yearly 
and annual financial results of the Company both on standalone and consolidated basis to the Stock Exchanges and publication 
of the same in both Vernacular and National newspapers and disclosure of presentations on Financial Results made to Institutional 
investors / analysts and to the Stock Exchanges. The same disclosures are also published on the website of the Company ( www.
natcopharma.co.in ).

Exchanges and updated on the Company’s website ( www.natcopharma.co.in ) as well as made part of press releases. Any price 
sensitive information is brought to the notice of both the Stock Exchanges (NSE and BSE), Press and Electronic Media in order to 
avoid any possible insider trading practices with such information.

7. Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets 
and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)
 At Natco Pharma Limited, we are committed to advancing healthcare through innovative, quality, and accessible specialty 
medicines. Our strong foundation in research and development enables us to address complex therapeutic needs while 
creating meaningful value for patients, partners, and society at large. Beyond delivering medicines, we strive to create a 
broader impact by embedding sustainability, responsibility, and inclusive growth into our core business strategy.
 Our ESG journey continues to evolve alongside emerging global challenges. As a manufacturing-driven pharmaceutical 
organization, we recognize climate change, resource efficiency, and regulatory expectations as key areas requiring sustained 
focus. In response, we have set clear environmental targets, including increasing the share of renewable energy in our overall 
energy mix to 35% by 2035 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. We are also advancing our water stewardship efforts, with 
a focus on achieving water neutrality at key facilities, alongside strengthening circular waste management practices.  
 On the social front, ensuring equitable access to affordable medicines, fostering an inclusive workplace, and contributing 
meaningfully to community development remain central to our approach. We continue to invest in employee well-being, 
diversity, and capability building, while expanding our community initiatives in healthcare, education, and social empowerment. 
Our commitment to product quality and patient safety remains unwavering, supported by responsible product stewardship 
across the value chain.
 From a governance perspective, we are focused on strengthening transparency, ethical conduct, and risk management 
practices in an increasingly complex business environment. We have implemented robust governance frameworks, reinforced 
responsible sourcing through our Sustainable Sourcing Policy, and are progressing towards ISO 27001 certification to enhance 
our information security systems.
 We have made steady progress across our ESG priorities, particularly in expanding renewable energy adoption, improving 
water recycling efficiency, and sustaining high levels of landfill diversion across the some of our manufacturing facilities. These 
achievements reflect our structured and disciplined approach towards integrating ESG into business operations.
 As we move forward, we remain focused on addressing evolving ESG challenges while delivering on our commitments 
with accountability and transparency. Our approach to healing beyond medicine reflects a broader responsibility—to drive 
innovation that not only improves patient outcomes but also contributes to a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient future 
for all stakeholders.

4. Does the entity have an anti-corruption or anti-bribery policy? If yes, provide details in brief and if available, 
provide a web-link to the policy. 
 -Yes.
 NATCO Pharma Limited upholds ethics, integrity, and transparency while ensuring compliance with applicable laws, rules, and 
regulations. This policy provides clear guidance for identifying and addressing ethical concerns, establishes mechanism for 
reporting misconduct, and promotes a culture of honesty and accountability. It applies to all employees, contractors, suppliers, 
and business partners. The policy strictly prohibits bribery, corruption, inappropriate gifts, manipulation, and concealment. 
Employees are encouraged to promptly report any suspected violations to their supervisor or the Compliance Officer. In 
addition, a comprehensive whistleblower framework supports this policy, enabling the safe and confidential reporting of 
unethical practices, suspected fraud, or breaches of the Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery policy.

2. Does the entity have processes in place to avoid/ manage conflict of interests involving members of the Board? 
(Yes/No) If yes, provide details of the same
 Yes,.
 The Company has established a comprehensive governance framework through its ‘Code of Conduct for Board Members, Senior 
Management Personnel and Employees’ policy, ‘Related Party Transactions’ Policy and ‘Nomination and Remuneration’ Policy 
to identify, prevent and manage conflicts of interest involving the Board of Directors and Key Management Personnel (KMPs).
 Under the ‘Code of Conduct for Board Members, Senior Management Personnel and Employees’ Policy, members of the 
Board are required to avoid situations that may result in actual or potential conflicts of interest with the Company's interests. In 
the event of any such conflict, or where a conflict is likely to arise, the concerned individual is required to make a full disclosure 
of all relevant facts to the Board of Directors or the authority designated by the Board and obtain prior written approval 
before proceeding.

3. Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling and disposing at the end 
of life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste.
 We adopt an eco-friendly approach to waste management by implementing well-defined Standard Operating Procedures 
(SOPs) for the collection, storage, and disposal of waste. The Company works with authorized agencies in compliance with 
CPCB/SPCB guidelines to ensure proper recycling, reuse, and environmentally safe disposal.
 a) Plastics (including packaging): The Company fulfils 100% of its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations 
for post-consumer plastic packaging waste through authorized third-party agencies, in accordance with CPCB/SPCB 
guidelines. This includes recycling, co-processing, and environmentally sound disposal of waste equivalent to the total 
quantity of packaging introduced in the market.
 b) E-waste: E-waste generated is handed over to authorized recyclers through collection centers or to authorized dismantlers 
for recycling, in line with the E-Waste Management Rules, 2022.
 c) Hazardous waste: Hazardous waste is sent to authorized cement industries, pre-processing facilities, or Treatment, 
Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDF) for safe and compliant disposal.
 d) Other waste: Other waste streams are directed to pre-processing facilities or recyclers for further processing and recycling.
4. Whether Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is applicable to the entity’s activities (Yes / No). If yes, whether 
the waste collection plan is in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to Pollution 
Control Boards? If not, provide steps taken to address the same.
 Yes, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is applicable to the organization’s operations. The Company is registered as 
a Brand Owner under the Plastic Waste Management Rules and has submitted an EPR Action Plan in accordance with 
CPCB guidelines.
 The EPR obligations are fulfilled through authorized third-party waste management agencies. During the reporting year, 163 
tons of post-consumer plastic packaging waste was managed through recycling, co-processing, and other environmentally 
sound disposal methods, in line with the approved plan submitted to the respective Pollution Control Boards.

10. Health and safety management system:
 a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). 
If yes, the coverage such system?
  Yes, NATCO Pharma has implemented a robust Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management System across 
all its operational sites. This system is governed by a comprehensive Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS) policy 
and is integrated into the company's core operations. We ensure that adequate resources are allocated to implement 
EHS programs aligned with regulatory requirements and business objectives. EHS goals are embedded into business 
planning, governance, and performance evaluation processes to reinforce a culture of safety. Regular safety trainings, 
mock drills, awareness campaigns, and inspections are conducted across sites. The company continuously monitors 
safety performance, conducts root cause analysis of incidents, and takes preventive and corrective actions to avoid 
recurrence. All of our manufacturing facilities, including the NATCO Research Centre (NRC), are certified under ISO 
14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018. Certification for the Crop Health Sciences unit is currently in progress.
 b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine 
basis by the entity?
  The entity adopts a comprehensive approach to identifying workplace hazards and assessing risks for both routine 
and non-routine activities. Key methodologies include HAZOP (Hazard and Operability Study), which systematically 
examines complex processes to identify potential hazards, and HIRA (Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment), which 
evaluates the level of risk associated with various tasks.
  In addition, detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have been established for all critical operations to ensure 
consistent and safe work practices. A robust Work Permit System is also implemented to control high-risk and non-
routine activities such as confined space entry, hot work, and work at heights, ensuring that all necessary safety 
precautions are in place prior to execution.
  These systems are further strengthened through regular audits, inspections, and employe training programs, supporting 
continuous improvement in workplace safety performance.
 c. Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove themselves from 
such risks. (Y/N)[
  Yes, we promote a strong safety-oriented mindset among workers as a key element of our occupational health and 
safety framework, with a firm commitment to achieving the goal of “Zero Injury.” Employees are regularly engaged 
through structured training programs, toolbox talks, and safety briefings to enhance awareness, reinforce safe work 
practices, and ensure clear understanding of safety procedures.
  A comprehensive guidance document is in place to support the identification, evaluation, and mitigation of Safety, 
Health, and Environment (SH&E) risks. It provides clear direction on risk assessment methodologies and defines the 
roles and responsibilities of both workers and supervisors in managing safety across all site activities. Workers are 
Corporate Overview177
Statutory Reports Financial Statements
=== page 132 ===
encouraged and empowered to report unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and near-misses, and they have the right to stop 
work if they believe it poses a serious risk to their safety or health. 
 d. Do the employees/workers of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/ No)
  Yes, each operational site is equipped with a fully functional Occupational Health Centre, supported by qualified 
doctor/s, nurses to monitor and promote the overall well-being of the workforce. In addition, the Company provides 
comprehensive health insurance coverage through its Group Medical Insurance policy and the Employee State Insurance 
Scheme (ESIC), ensuring access to a wide range of healthcare services beyond occupational requirements.

12. Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy workplace.
 We operate a comprehensive Occupational Health and Safety Management System aligned with ISO 45001 standards. 
Regular Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) exercises are conducted to identify potential workplace hazards 
and implement appropriate control measures. A stringent Permit-to-Work (PTW) system is in place to govern all high-risk 
operational and maintenance activities. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is provided and mandated for employees and 
workers based on the risk profile of their tasks.
 At our manufacturing facilities, scrubber systems and other emission control technologies are deployed to minimize exposure 
to volatile organic compounds (VOCs), dust, and odours. Fire safety is ensured through well-maintained fire detection and 
alarm systems, adequate fire-fighting equipment, and periodic fire drills to strengthen emergency preparedness. Regular 
safety inspections, surveillance activities, and internal audits are conducted to ensure compliance and identify opportunities 
for continual improvement. In addition, exposure assessments and Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) studies are carried 
out, as needed. 
 We provide regular health and safety training to all employees and workers, along with emergency preparedness drills for 
scenarios such as chemical spills and fire incidents. Periodic medical examinations are conducted by reputed health care 
facilities, including specialized health checkups as per the need A fully equipped Occupational Health Centre (OHC) is available 
at all sites, supported by a qualified doctor and nurse to provide immediate on-site medical assistance.

15. Provide details of any corrective action taken or underway to address safety-related incidents (if any) and on 
significant risks/concerns arising from assessments of health & safety practices and working conditions.
 At NATCO, we are strongly committed to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment across all our operations. Regular 
internal audits are conducted to assess safety performance, and appropriate corrective actions are implemented based on 
audit findings. To enhance fire safety preparedness, auto modular-type fire extinguishing systems have been installed in 
critical areas to ensure rapid response during emergencies.
 We have undertaken detailed assessments of solids charging operations, leading to the adoption of reverse charging systems 
wherever applicable. In addition, solids charging hoppers have been fitted with double flap valve arrangements to improve 
operational safety and reduce exposure risks.
 To further strengthen process safety, HAZOP (Hazard and Operability) studies are conducted to proactively identify and 
mitigate potential hazards. Employees receive regular training, first aid, and emergency response, delivered through certified 
external agencies. Periodic fire drills are also conducted to ensure readiness. Furthermore, Environment, Health, and Safety 
(EHS) awareness campaigns are carried out across facilities to promote a strong culture of safety.

5. Has the entity implemented a mechanism for Zero Liquid Discharge? If yes, provide details of its coverage and 
implementation.
 Yes, we have implemented Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems at four of our manufacturing plants to ensure effective 
wastewater management and  environmental compliance. The ZLD approach is aimed for effective onsite treatment and reuse 
resulting into reduction of fresh water footprint and achieving zero discharge from the premises.
 The plants with ZLD systems are located at  Mekaguda (Telangana), Kothur (Telangana), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), and Athivaram 
Technical (Andhra Pradesh), with treated water of 58,810 KL, 42,285.06 KL, 11,093.04 KL, and 1,244 KL respectively. The 
treated water is fully reused for cooling towers, sanitation (toilets), and gardening, contributing to our water conservation and 
sustainability goals.

10. Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy 
adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes, 
and the practices adopted to manage such wastes.[.
 NATCO Pharma implements a comprehensive waste management plan focused on minimization, segregation, and safe 
disposal. The company adopts a green chemistry approach to optimize the use of hazardous chemicals and ensures 
responsible waste handling.
 1. Hazardous Waste: Managed through co-processing in authorized cement industries, treatment at certified pre-processing 
facilities, and disposal in TSDFs. Used oil, e-waste, and batteries are sent to licensed recyclers or managed through 
structured buy-back programs.
 2. Non-Hazardous Waste: Combustible waste undergoes pre-processing before co-processing in cement kilns, paper 
waste is sent to ITC for recycling, and metal scrap is handled by authorized recyclers. Plastic waste is managed under 
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) initiatives.
 3. Biodegradable Waste: Processed through organic waste converters to produce compost for facility landscaping.
 4. Effluent & Sewage Treatment: ZLD, ETP and STP systems to treat the waste water to meet environmental 
compliance standards.

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/ web link.
 At NATCO Pharma, the Business Continuity and Disaster Management Plan forms an integral component of the overall Risk 
Management Framework, designed to ensure operational resilience across all business units and functions during unforeseen 
disruptions. Aligned with the Company’s Risk Management Policy—which identifies environmental risks as a key focus area—
the plan outlines comprehensive strategies to mitigate and manage risks that may impact business continuity. It details 
emergency preparedness measures, including control protocols and response procedures, while addressing critical aspects 
such as environmental risk assessments, evacuation plans, shutdown procedures, and emergency coordination structures.
 To facilitate timely and coordinated response, clear roles and responsibilities are defined, supported by designated assembly 
points, access to medical facilities, availability of safety documentation (MSDS), and established communication channels 
with external and mutual aid partners. In addition, all personnel, including contract workers, undergo regular training to 
strengthen preparedness for emergency situations.
 This structured and multi-layered approach reflects NATCO Pharma’s commitment to operational continuity, environmental 
responsibility, and organizational resilience, in alignment with its broader risk governance framework.

 During the reporting periods, the Company did not encounter any significant adverse environmental impact incidents attributable

commitment to sustainable and responsible sourcing practices across the supply chain. Our Sustainable Procurement Policy 
focuses on minimizing environmental impact across its value chain. This policy acknowledges areas where sustainability

5. Does the entity have a framework/policy on cyber security and risks related to data privacy? If available, provide 
a web link to the policy.
 Yes, NATCO Pharma Limited has established a comprehensive Data Privacy and Cybersecurity Policy that defines its approach 
to safeguarding sensitive information and mitigating cyber risks. The framework encompasses governance, access control, 
risk mitigation, and compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements. Oversight is exercised by senior leadership 
and the IT Security function, ensuring effective implementation and periodic review of the policy.
 Confidential information—including employee records, business data, and contractual documents—is protected through 
stringent access controls, with permissions granted strictly on a need-to-know basis to authorized personnel. The Company 
has implemented Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tools and robust cybersecurity protocols to prevent unauthorized access, data 
leakage, or breaches, whether internal or external. All users of the Company’s IT systems are required to adhere to defined 
guidelines to prevent unauthorized data sharing or misuse.
 Established incident response mechanisms enable the timely detection, investigation, and resolution of potential cybersecurity 
threats or data breaches. Employees are regularly sensitized through training programs on cybersecurity awareness and their 
responsibilities under the policy framework.
 The policy is reviewed on periodic basis to ensure continued alignment with evolving regulatory requirements and emerging 
cybersecurity risks, thereby reinforcing the Company’s commitment to data protection and information security.
 Policy web-link – Data Privacy and Cyber Security Policy
